subject: Getting dplyr's group_by output to be as clearly labeled as dlply's

messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: Getting dplyr's group_by output to be as clearly labeled as dlply's
parts:
Hi All,

I hope I'm missing something simple regarding how dplyr labels group_by output. Below is an example that shows that the way I'm doing it, groups are labeled with [[n]] in dplyr while dlply uses clear group labels.

Thanks,
Bob

# Create some data.
gender <- sample(c("Male","Female"), 100, replace = TRUE)
treatment  <- sample(LETTERS[1:4], 100, replace = TRUE)
score  <- rnorm(100)
df <- data.frame(gender, treatment, score)
head(df)

# This uses plyr to get t.tests that compare genders
# for each treatment level. The output is clearly
# labeled by treatment (my goal).
myfun <- function(x) {
  with(x,
       t.test(score ~ gender)
  )
}
library("plyr")
dlply(df, .(treatment), myfun)
detach("package:plyr")


# Next I do the same thing using dplyr
library("dplyr")
my.t.tests <-
  df %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  do(
    mod = t.test(score ~ gender, data = .)
  )

# This shows treatment name, but not results
my.t.tests

# This shows results, but not treatment name
my.t.tests[[2]]

# This assigns group name to results
# so the output is finally easy to read,
# just like output from dlply.
# Is there some simple approach to displaying
# output that I'm missing? 
names(my.t.tests[[2]]) <- my.t.tests[[1]]
my.t.tests[[2]]
detach("package:dplyr")

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Getting dplyr's group_by output to be as clearly labeled as dlply's
parts:
Hi Bob,

The expectation is that you'd use summarise() or mutate() to extract
the bits of the model object and keep them associated with names,
e.g.:

my.t.tests %>% summarise(pval = mod$p.value)

Unfortunately this doesn't preserve the labels either, but it's
something that I want to figure out for the next version of dplyr.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Getting dplyr's group_by output to be as clearly labeled as dlply's
parts:
Hi Hadley,

Thanks for the clarification. If I have many groups, the lack of labels makes it very difficult to track which is which. Putting them in the names attribute isn't hard, but it makes beginner's eyes glaze over. For the moment I've regressed all way back to using by() for this when teaching beginners. Most people are looking for printed results by group & by() not only does the labels but it also won't choke on NAs. My usual SAS migrators are familiar with the "by" term too.

I followed your example and got most of the output I was seeking, but got stuck where the t.test means are in a vector. I must be missing something really basic (example below). Any ideas?

Thanks,
Bob



As long as I don't ask for means, I'm all set:

> summarise(my.t.tests,
+           t    = mod$statistic,
+           df   = mod$parameter,
+           pval = mod$p.value)
Source: local data frame [4 x 3]

         t     df      pval
1 -1.44987 13.743 0.1695313
2  2.87528 23.251 0.0084915
3  0.61574 19.712 0.5451081
4  1.32842 10.361 0.2125571
> summarise(my.t.tests,
+           female = mod$estimate[1],
+           male   = mod$estimate[2])
Error in summarise_impl(.data, named_dots(...), environment()) : 
  object 'mod' not found

The means are definitely in the estimate[1] and estimate[2] positions:

> my.t.tests[[2]]$A$p.value
[1] 0.16953
> my.t.tests[[2]]$A$parameter  # df
    df 
13.743 
> my.t.tests[[2]]$A$p.value
[1] 0.16953
> my.t.tests[[2]]$A$estimate # both means
mean in group Female   mean in group Male 
             0.20864              0.93540 
> my.t.tests[[2]]$A$estimate[1]  # female mean
mean in group Female 
             0.20864 
> my.t.tests[[2]]$A$estimate[2]  #   male mean
mean in group Male 
            0.9354
